description:
The capability keys a call digest must carry, and what each one asserts. Kept as data so the producer, the UI and the conformance suite read one list rather than three.

A capability reflects measured evidence and producer support — not whether a schema field exists. A field present and null because nothing was measured is `unavailable`, not `available`. This is the mechanism that keeps a missing section from rendering as a healthy one.

keys.usage: Participant sessions, peak concurrency, observed and connected participant time. Partial when membership intervals are known for only some participants.
keys.joinOutcomes: Application join attempts and their outcomes. Unavailable without a versioned attempt adapter — a peer connection is not a join attempt.
keys.audio: Inbound audio quality evaluation: loss, jitter, concealment, jitter buffer delay.
keys.video: Inbound and outbound video quality evaluation: loss, freeze, FPS, encode and decode cost, encoder limitation.
keys.network: Transport-level loss and round-trip time on the selected path.
keys.connectivity: Connection-state evidence: whether disconnection and failure can be observed at all.
keys.paths: Selected ICE path reconstruction — relay, protocol, and the server actually serving each interval. Unavailable where the producer's retained on-change metadata cannot establish it.
keys.topology: Publisher-to-subscriber relationships. Unavailable unless verified signalling or resolver evidence supports the links; equal SSRC alone never establishes one.
keys.cohorts: Dimension attribution for this call's participants.
keys.scores: Observer summary score metadata. Explicitly NOT a measured quality metric in v1: a native producer's default score of 5 is a default, not a healthy measurement, and scores are never fed into fleet means or percentiles.

scoresNote: v1 requires no overall score. Existing Observer score min/max/median may be surfaced as clearly labelled source-summary metadata through a future additive section. They may not enter any aggregate on any screen.
